reader.requirement: In a contained program B, the candidate set for a condition-name, data-name, file-name, record-name or report-name reference is B's own names plus the GLOBAL names of every directly or indirectly containing program (never a container's non-global names), and qualification is applied over that whole set.

edition-consulted.switches: only the citation text of the ambiguity diagnostic (DialectLevel < 2002 cites §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.1); the candidate set and the refusal are the same code

reader.edition-search: grep EditionContext|CobolVersion|DialectLevel|ConstructRegistry in SymbolTable.cs, InheritStep.cs, InheritedGlobals.cs, DataBinder.NonDataNames.cs, ReportScope.cs: none; the inheritance and nearest-tier narrowing are edition-free. The GLOBAL clause itself is admitted at --std 85 (every probe compiled).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb1047 covers data-names, condition-names and index-names inherited from two container levels; not exercised: a container's NON-global name of the same spelling (excluded from the set), a global FILE-name and record-name against a contained program's own file of the same name, and the refusal of a reference to a container's non-global name

probes.printed: M X=MNX K=MNK / I X=OGX / I YG=OGY / I K=OHK / I KH=OHK / I ZG=IGZ / O Y=NEW K=NWK
probes.expected: the middle program's non-global X and H.K are not in the inner program's set, so X and K name the outer GLOBAL items; Y OF G is qualified over the whole set (the inner G holds no Y) and names the outer Y; the MOVEs write the outer items
the outer program's non-global Q is not in the contained program's set: the reference identifies nothing and is refused

probes.printed: O R=GLBJ / O R=EOF; g1fi.dat holds LOCI, g1fo.dat holds GLBJ
probes.expected: the contained program with its own FD F writes its own file; the one without writes the container's GLOBAL F and its record R

probes.printed: error COBOL1639: 'X' does not uniquely identify a data item (ISO §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.1)
probes.expected: two local X plus a global X: qualification over the set leaves more than one object local to B, so the reference is not unique

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.1.3.8.2 GR1  (1.3.8.2 Conventions for Condition-Names, Data-Names, File-Names, Record-Names, and Report-Names)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: Every container's GLOBAL roots (and their subordinates, condition-names, RENAMES and index-names) are inherited with their containment depth after the unit's own names; a container's non-global names never enter the set. Qualification runs over the whole set before the nearest-tier narrowing (GR3), so Y OF G reaches the outer G's Y past a local G without it. The only edition consultation is the citation in the ambiguity text.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-233/src): g_rpt2.cob: a container's GLOBAL RD RPT (with GLOBAL FD) is reached by INITIATE/GENERATE/TERMINATE in a contained program with no RD (gro.txt holds OUTR), and a sibling's local RD RPT is its own (grl.txt holds LOCL): report-names are in the set. g_sib.cob: a GLOBAL item of a sibling (not a container) is refused COBOL1639 'SX' is not defined. g_down.cob: the container cannot reference its contained program's GLOBAL item (COBOL1639). g_cond.cob: B's local record-name R (FD record) hides the container's global data-name R (MOVE writes B's, outer R stays OWR). The reader's g1set/g1nonglobal/g1file cover non-global exclusion and file-names. cite.py: OK §1985:X.1.3.8.2 GR1 the text is in GR1; OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1 the text is in the clause (condition-names, data-names, and record-names form one set). Wording only: COBOL1639 at --std 85 cites §2023:8.4.2.1, not a 1985 rule.
